summary: Port BROT's gemma-prompting patterns to Sage prompt-side only: reserved status property on every tool schema, TUTOR_TOOL_GUIDANCE system block (tool-use rules, status fill, voice continuity, generalized advancement/anti-repetition), model-written status passthrough on SSE tool_call events, client prefers model-authored status over hardcoded name mapping, scripted test extended.
final_report:
T70 complete - BROT's proven gemma-prompting patterns applied to Sage, prompt-side only, zero enforcement/scrubbing code added. This replaces hardcoded client-side tool statuses with model-authored ones wherever the model provides a status.

[1] app/llm/tools.py - reserved "status" string property with BROT-style description ('Short, warm, user-facing description of what you are doing right now, shown live while the tool runs. Example: Searching for a reliable definition.... Not hidden reasoning.') injected into EVERY tool schema via the _fn builder (_STATUS_PROP merged into properties, never required) so all six tools (web_search, generate_mermaid, generate_quiz, generate_todo, generate_latex, record_step_actions) carry it, including any future ones.

[2] app/llm/messages.py - new TUTOR_TOOL_GUIDANCE block inside APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS (~7 sentences, modeled on BROT's TOOL_USAGE_GUIDANCE + VOICE_CONTINUITY_GUIDANCE): per-tool usage rules (generate_* only when asked or clearly helpful, web_search only when sources genuinely needed, record_step_actions ONCE per teaching step), do-not-call-unneeded-tools, reserved-status fill rule, voice continuity after tool results (still Sage, same lesson, few sentences, never restart/re-introduce), and the generalized anti-repetition advancement rule (never restate earlier material; back-reference like 'as with the dolls example'; each turn teaches something new). Judgment call flagged in notes: thin TOOL_HINT constant REPLACED by this block rather than kept alongside it - it subsumed every TOOL_HINT rule incl. 'never fabricate tool output'; strict/grounded grounding semantics untouched. Dolls handling is now prompt-only as directed.

[3] app/services/sessions/turn.py - SSE tool_call event now passes through arguments.get("status") as top-level event field when it is a non-blank string (whitespace-only treated as absent); no other loop changes.

[4] static/sage-workspace.html - tool_status_text() prefers ev.status (model-written, trimmed) and falls back to the existing hardcoded TOOL_STATUS name map / generic 'running X...' text only when absent.

[5] tests/test_tools_loop.py - scripted FakeLLM web_search fixture arguments now include "status":"Looking up sources..."; assertions extended to cover both the arguments echo and the yielded SSE tool_call dict carrying status passthrough.

Verification: python -m compileall -q app OK; pytest tests/test_tools_loop.py -q -> 10 passed in 5.20s; node --check on all 5 extracted <script> blocks of sage-workspace.html rc=0 (block 4, 37,887 bytes, contains the changed function). Pre-existing LSP type noise in turn.py/client.py/fake_llm.py/test_tools_loop.py unchanged and unrelated (documented in T62/T66).

Diff-vs-base caveat for Orpheus: git diff against base_commit additionally shows removal of the T48 dolls-scrub machinery (DOLLS_MARKERS, scrub_analogy_sentencewise, scrub_history_analogies, allow_first_analogy) from messages.py/turn.py - that removal pre-existed my session in the uncommitted working tree (my first read of both files already lacked it; git status listed them modified before I edited). I made no scrub-related edits; repo-wide grep finds zero remaining references to those symbols, so the tree is self-consistent. line_counts.before are raw wc -l semantics of the working tree I edited from (Python splitlines fallback per oc-issues #31); static/ is untracked so it has no HEAD baseline. No concurrent writer touched my files mid-task (only stale T48 log existed, superseded by this task's prompt-side-only directive); no reconciliation needed. No commit.
